insight.title: What the world is made of when nobody is looking
insight.subtitle: The elegant architecture of the space between us.

sections.text: Look at the palms of your hands. They feel solid, heavy, and permanent. Yet, nature hides a quiet secret about the fabric of our world. Almost everything you see is made of nothing at all. If we removed the empty space from every human, our entire species would fit inside a single sugar cube.

The atoms that build your body are like miniature, silent solar systems. Each one is a vast cathedral with a tiny center. They only feel solid because invisible fields push back against your fingers. You never truly touch a lover’s hand; you simply hover near it, held apart by a microscopic, electric push.

This hidden architecture changes how we view the mundane. We are not heavy sculptures of clay, but light, intricate clouds of energy. It is a beautiful irony that the things we find most substantial are mostly made of ghosts. In a vast emptiness, the simple act of holding on is the greatest miracle of all.

news.title: Indian banks likely to face margin pressure amid tighter liquidity in FY27: Fitch
news.description: Indian banks may see tighter margins. The Reserve Bank of India faces challenges injecting funds due to rupee volatility. Global risks could further impact bank earnings. Despite this, Indian banks are seen as resilient. Liquidity surplus in the banking system has decreased. Rupee pressure could limit the RBI's policy options. Direct foreign currency risks for banks remain limited.
